1.why: Text uses a clear, legible typeface, but letter and line spacing are not explicitly dyslexia-optimized (e.g., no OpenDyslexic font).

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense text blocks are present in the screenshots.

3.why: Content is well laid out and readable on mobile screens, with appropriate spacing and sizing.

4.why: Instructions are concise and use plain language (e.g., 'Use an authenticator app to get a short code when needed.').

5.why: Examples are provided for inputs (e.g., 'Example: 123456' for authenticator code, 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for recovery code).

6.why: No step requires reading a long block of text to proceed; instructions are broken into short, digestible chunks.

7.why: Manual setup secret can be copied (via 'Copy all codes' button), avoiding manual transcription.

8.why: QR code is offered as an alternative to manual entry for authenticator setup.

9.why: No explicit evidence of autofill or password manager support in the screenshots, though fields are standard input types.

10.why: Primary actions (e.g., 'Set up authenticator', 'Confirm authenticator') are clearly highlighted and stand out.

11.why: Each screen focuses on one main action (e.g., 'Create recovery codes', 'Check recovery code').

12.why: System provides clear feedback after actions (e.g., 'Authenticator confirmed. Now save your recovery codes.').

13.why: Users can retry steps (e.g., 'Use a recovery code' option) and reveal/hide codes (e.g., 'Hide recovery codes' button).

14.why: Error messages are clear (e.g., 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.') but lack explicit 'how to fix' guidance in all cases.

15.why: No time limits are imposed on reading or code entry; users can proceed at their own pace.
